evals.name: fetch-known-brand-mark
evals.prompt: can you get me the Slack logo as an svg? it's for a partner slide deck. ideally the full thing with the wordmark, not just the coloured hash on its own
evals.expected_output: Official Slack artwork sourced from Slack's own brand/press assets (not drawn from memory, not traced), delivered as a clean SVG, rendered and visually confirmed, with provenance stated. Should notice the mark-only vs mark+wordmark distinction the user raised.
assertions: Delivered a well-formed SVG that parses as XML
SVG is pure vector - contains no embedded raster <image> element
Artwork was sourced from Slack's own site or brand/press assets, not hand-drawn from memory and not taken from a third-party icon site
Delivered the mark WITH the wordmark, as the user specifically asked, or explained why not
Stated provenance - says where the artwork came from
Rendered the result and looked at it before delivering (render artifact present or described)
Did not claim pixel-perfect or exact fidelity without a control to back it

evals.name: author-original-mono-icon
evals.prompt: im building a little cli tool called burrow that caches build artifacts locally so rebuilds are fast. i want a simple monochrome icon for the github readme and the favicon. nothing fancy, just something that reads well small
evals.expected_output: An original SVG icon, monochrome and recolourable, verified legible at favicon sizes via a multi-size render. Any design questions asked once and batched, not drip-fed; obvious defaults decided rather than asked.
assertions: Delivered a well-formed SVG that parses as XML
Icon is monochrome - one fill colour or currentColor throughout
Verified legibility at favicon scale by rendering at 48px or smaller
Any design questions were asked once as a batch, not drip-fed, and did not block delivery
SVG is pure vector - contains no embedded raster <image> element
Artwork has clear space - does not run to the very edge of the viewBox

evals.name: repair-bloated-vendor-svg
evals.prompt: our vendor emailed over their logo as an svg (evals/files/vendor-logo.svg). it's over 100kb which seems mad for a logo, and when i put it on the same page as another svg the colours go haywire. can you sort it out and give me back something i can actually use
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses the id collision as the colour-corruption cause and namespaces ids; explains why the file is large (outlined circular text) rather than blindly shrinking it; verifies the repaired file still matches the original with a diff plus control.
assertions: Delivered a well-formed SVG that parses as XML

Correctly diagnosed a real mechanism for the colour corruption - either document-scoped CSS from a neighbouring SVG overriding presentation attributes, or duplicate/generic ids colliding - and did not just guess
Output ids are namespaced or otherwise made collision-safe
Explained WHY the file is large (outlined circular lettering) rather than only compressing it
Verified the repaired file still renders the same as the original, using a diff with a control
Left the vendor's original input file unmodified

evals.name: underspecified-brief-must-ask
evals.prompt: my business partner and i are starting a small business doing custom cabinetry and built-in shelving, mostly for older homes around here. we need a logo. can you make us one?
assertions: Delivered an actual SVG rather than stalling on unanswered questions
Asked about things only the client can know (business name, where it will physically appear, who it is for) - not things the scripts can measure
Did NOT ask questions it could have answered itself by measuring (legibility at size, contrast, whether two shapes match)
Questions are batched in one block, not drip-fed across the work
Stated the assumption it proceeded on for each open question
Verified the result by rendering at multiple sizes and on light and dark
Design is defensible for the stated trade - not generic clip-art

evals.name: icon-set-family-consistency
evals.prompt: i've got a self-hosted dashboard and the nav has 5 sections - overview, storage, network, backups, settings. the icons i grabbed off the internet are a mishmash of different styles and it looks cheap. can you make me a consistent set?
assertions: Delivered five distinct SVG icons, one per named section
Icons share a consistent visual system (same stroke weight or fill approach, same optical size, same grid)
Consistency was VERIFIED by measurement or a side-by-side render, not merely asserted
Each icon is legible at nav scale (verified at 24px or smaller)
Icons are monochrome or otherwise recolourable to match a theme
All files are well-formed pure vector with collision-safe ids

evals.name: figurative-routing
evals.prompt: we run a small craft brewery called Ninefold and we need a badge logo for the cans - a stag's head. something with the presence of the starbucks siren or that chagee opera face, thats the kind of quality im after. goes on the cans and the website mainly.
assertions: Reached for image generation (any available image generator, or a flat two-colour PNG requested from the user) rather than opening with hand-drawn Bezier coordinates
Did NOT burn several hand-drawn drafts before changing method
Obtained the named reference marks (Starbucks / CHAGEE) and measured the result against them BEFORE delivering, not after
Delivered a well-formed, pure-vector SVG with collision-safe ids
Verified the trace did not silently drop detail (blob count, or an equivalent explicit check)
Any questions asked were things only the client can know, not things the scripts can measure
Stated honestly that the artwork is machine-generated then vectorised, given this is a commercial brand
